item.title: 'We all made mistakes': Darren Lehmann stands by Sandpapergate version, reveals 'dark place' after 2018 scandal
item.description: The Sandpapergate controversy continues to haunt Australian cricket, with former coach Darren Lehmann once again insisting that he had no knowledge of the ball-tampering plot during the 2018 South Africa tour. Acknowledging that the scandal was a dark chapter for everyone involved, Lehmann said he accepted responsibility as coach but stood by his version of events. Speaking to ABC Radio ahead of the first T20I between Australia and England on Saturday, Lehmann said the controversy had taken a severe personal toll but maintained that his account had not changed. "I haven't changed my views from what happened in 2018," Lehmann said. "It was a dark time, and we got a lot of things wrong, but my version still stays the same. It was just a bad time. We all made mistakes." The former Australia coach's comments come amid renewed scrutiny of the scandal following Usman Khawaja's claim that "all of us" knew about the ball-tampering plan and Cameron Bancroft's detailed account of the events in a 4,000-word article. Coach Darren Lehmann was also present." The former Australia opener also alleged that David Warner "raised the possibility of using sandpaper to roughen one side of the ball". Lehmann also reflected on the distinction between conventional ball maintenance and what happened during the 2018 scandal. item.title: Mike Pettine Can, and Should, Turn Tide for the Cowboys
item.description: So, the Dallas Cowboys are in turmoil… again. In a year full of Cowboys surprises, both good and bad, the biggest one has somehow been the defense. After a historically bad 2025, no one expected Dallas to be any worse in 2026. Hiring former Eagles DB coach Christian Parker as the defensive coordinator gave the Dallas faithful even more hope for the defense. It’s now less than a week until Thanksgiving, and the defense is so horrendous to the point that Parker has been relieved of his duties as the defensive play-caller. Not a single Cowboys fan had that on their bingo card for the year. Now, in steps defensive assistant Mike Pettine to try and save the day. His mission starts on Sunday against the Titans, a game many people don’t see as a measuring stick for improvement. I can already see it now: DAL fires/takes away play-calling duties from Christian Parker, and DAL's defense performs adequately against the Terribad Titans (TT) and Egregious Eagles (EE), so everyone hurts their hands giving each other high-fives before the defense inevitably… — John Owning (@JohnOwning) November 17, 2026 However, just because the Tennessee Titans aren’t a prolific offensive powerhouse doesn’t mean Pettine can’t show what he’s got from day one. There are various ways to measure improvement, and Pettine will have to measure up quickly. Old Soul ‘Round the Block Before getting to how he’ll be tested, it’d be good to know exactly who the Cowboy faithful are putting the fate of the defense behind. Mike Pettine has been coaching for as long as some of his players have been alive. Starting in 2002 with the Baltimore Ravens, Pettine has spent the last 24 seasons alternating between defensive assistant, linebacker coach, and his new role with the Cowboys as the defensive play caller. He’s got good history, too—the New York Jets’ best defenses of the century (2009/10) came with Pettine overseeing duties as the DC. Regarding that role specifically, Pettine made stops in Buffalo and Green Bay to fill it. Both stops had a mixed bag of results. He lasted a year in Buffalo, posting an average defense, and in Green Bay he lasted three, with good defenses and two NFC Title trips. Now, he’s here to try and rescue the Cowboys. item.title: Cal answers Tamilo’s third-quarter surge, beats Hawaiʻi 70-49 in North Shore Showcase
item.description: LĀʻIE, Hawaiʻi — Ritorya Tamilo scored five points in 21 seconds to pull Hawaiʻi within four of unbeaten California late in the third quarter Friday. Zara Russell answered with a layup, and the Golden Bears closed the period on an 11-2 run to pull away for a 70-49 victory in the North Shore Showcase opener at the Cannon Activities Center. Tamilo finished with 16 points, seven rebounds and four blocks for the Rainbow Wahine (1-4). The junior center made a career-high three 3-pointers, including the one that cut Cal’s lead to 41-37 with 3:50 left in the third. Jovi Lefotu, who set up both Tamilo baskets during that stretch, scored a season-high 11 points and had five assists. Cal (6-0) played without leading scorer Lulu Twidale and got 33 points from its bench to Hawaiʻi’s seven. Center Albina Syla scored 16 points on 8-of-12 shooting and grabbed nine rebounds as the Bears outscored Hawaiʻi 40-20 in the paint. Russell added 14 points and seven rebounds off the bench, and fellow reserve Naya Ojukwu finished with 10 points and five rebounds. Russell helped the Bears build their first lead of consequence. In the closing seconds of the first quarter, Taylor Barnes drove the baseline and found Russell in the corner for a buzzer-beating 3-pointer that put Cal ahead 19-10. Hawaiʻi trailed 29-19 with just over four minutes left in the half, then scored eight straight points, the last two on a short jumper by Rebecca Moors. Cal took a 31-27 lead into halftime, and Tamilo scored inside to bring Hawaiʻi within two again on its first basket of the third quarter. Tamilo’s third 3-pointer gave the Rainbow Wahine one more chance to catch Cal. After Russell answered, Ojukwu converted a three-point play as the Bears stretched their lead to 52-39 by the end of the quarter. Hawaiʻi made just three of 16 shots in the fourth and finished 4 of 18 from beyond the arc. Guard Bailey Flavell scored five points on 1-of-12 shooting. The Rainbow Wahine close the showcase Saturday against Gonzaga. Tipoff is set for 2 p.m. Hawaiʻi time at the Cannon Activities Center.

item.title: Ampadu urges Leeds to build on 4-1 Chelsea win as European ambitions grow
item.description: Ampadu urges Leeds to build on 4-1 Chelsea win as European ambitions grow Ethan Ampadu has said Leeds United must build on the club's 4-1 win at Chelsea amid talk of competing for European football. Leeds produced a brilliant performance to thrash Chelsea and climb into the Premier League's top six. Daniel Farke's side fell behind to Emmanuel Emegha's first Chelsea goal, but roared back to claim a first win at Chelsea in 27 years. Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds, either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin spot-kick, before Brenden Aaronson sealed an emphatic success in the capital. Leeds had not beaten Chelsea at Stamford Bridge since December 1999, when Stephen McPhail scored twice in a 2-0 success. Reflecting on the win, Ampadu said the side were well aware of Leeds' poor recent record against their fierce rivals. "We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It's right we can enjoy this performance." Ampadu says Leeds ready for 'long road' to Europe after Chelsea win Leeds sit in the top six ahead of the weekend's remaining games, and Ampadu said there is an ambition in the squad to return to European football. However, he said Leeds must remain 'realistic' in that pursuit, and urged his side to find consistency in their performances. Leeds have not played in European competition since 2002/03. "We have to be realistic and understand how hard this league is. We need to back this up next week, if we don't then this performance is wasted. We know where we want to get Leeds back to. It could be a long road but we're ready for it."

item.title: Jersey Bulls cruise to impressive Littlehampton win
item.description: Jersey Bulls secured their biggest win of the season [BBC] Jersey Bulls recorded their biggest win of the season as they thrashed bottom-of-the-table Littlehampton Town 6-0. The win keeps the island second in Isthmian League South Central, two points behind Egham Town with a game in hand,. It means Bulls face third-placed Bognor Regis Town next week on their back of their biggest league win since an 8-1 victory at Chipstead in the Combined Counties League Premier Division in December 2024. Top scorner Lorne Bickley gave the Bulls an excellent start as he lobbed goalkeeper Billy Collings from an angle on the right of the box after seven-and-a-half minutes. Two minutes later Bickley got his second as he tapped in from close range after superb work from James Sunley to get to the byline and cut the ball back. Bulls almost made it 3-0 when James Queree had a 17th-minute header superbly saved by Collings. It was 3-0 13 minutes later when Jonny Le Quesne volleyed in a flicked-on throw before Sunley powered in the fourth from just inside the box six minutes later. Bickley completed his hat-trick five minutes from the break as he smashed in a right-footed effort from the edge of the box to make it 5-0. Sammy Henia-Kamau managed to miss an open goal from a Toby Ritzema cross just before the break. Jarma Mohamed - who played for Somalia against Ghana in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier in midweek - made it 6-0 after an hour when the substitute found the net seconds after coming on. Henia-Kamau had a couple more chances as the half wore on as the Bulls comfortably went home with three points. "We were ruthless," Jersey Bulls manager Elliot Powell told BBC Radio Jersey. "There was a spell when the game was relatively even, but every chance we got really we took, and when you've got a striker in the form that Lorne's in that tends to happen for you. "Long may that continue, we needed that, we needed a win away from home, but we also needed the win to set up next week against Bognor, so I'm delighted with it." Related internet links Jersey Bulls

item.description: Manchester City's Erling Haaland reacts during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. It was enough to end City’s run of three successive Premier League defeats but left them without a win in the competition for five weeks after opening the campaign with seven wins in a row. The main talking point was Haaland’s disallowed goal after 25 minutes, when the Norwegian prodded home from close range after a fumble by Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno. item.title: Man City boss Maresca says Erling Haaland had goal wrongly disallowed
item.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca reacts after conceding a goal to Fulham's Rodrigo Muniz during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Man City boss Maresca says Erling Haaland had goal wrongly disallowed») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca had no doubt Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal in Manchester City’s 1-1 draw with Fulham on Saturday should have stood. The prolific Norwegian had an effort chalked off in the Premier League encounter at the Etihad Stadium when he was deemed to have kicked the ball out of Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno’s hands. Haaland had not connected cleanly with a volley but Leno spilled the ball attempting to gather his attempt and the striker prodded in from close range. Referee Thomas Bramall, however, ruled that Leno – because the ball was still between his hands – had not lost control and VAR Sam Barrott upheld the decision. Maresca said: “I reviewed the goal after the game. From my point of view, it’s quite clear that it’s not a foul, but I’m not the guy that decides, unfortunately.” Asked how Haaland viewed the incident, Maresca added: “When they were reviewing the VAR, he was absolutely sure that it was a goal, because I asked him from the touchline. He was completely sure that it was a goal but the referee decided for different things.” With that effort ruled out in the 25th minute, City had to wait until just before the hour to cancel out Rodrigo Muniz’s 16th-minute opener. Elliot Anderson scored their equalizer with a fine volley – a sweet moment for the midfielder after being sent off playing for England last weekend. Maresca said: “It was a nice moment for him, a nice moment for us because it gave us the chance to come back in the game. “We used him today for the first time as an attacking midfielder. He was playing a little bit more deep with us. We are trying to find different solutions, the right balance, and to be more consistent.” Anderson’s equalizer ended City’s run of three successive Premier League defeats but it was nevertheless another frustrating result for a side that opened the campaign with seven straight wins. item.title: Trinity Rodman's healthiest season yet has her one win away from another NWSL title
item.description: WASHINGTON — We've all heard the saying: "The best ability is availability." That sports motto rings true more than ever for Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman. After being limited to a career-low 17 matches last season due to back and knee injuries, she bounced back with a career year that included personal highs in both goals (14) and assists (10). But that's not the most important accomplishment for Rodman, because if you strip away the highlight-reel goals and viral celebrations, she said she's just pleased to have played in a career-high 32 matches this season. The thought alone makes Rodman emotional. "It makes me want to cry," added the 24-year-old. "Just being able to be available, I don't think people realize how much of a blessing it is to be healthy enough to play. And I don't think you realize that until you go through something where it keeps you from doing something you love to do." Her 33rd game of the season will be the 2026 NWSL Championship, where the Spirit will face the Kansas City Current in their third consecutive finals appearance after finishing as a runner-up in the past two seasons. But unlike the last two finals when Rodman was impacted by injury, she's completely healthy heading into Saturday. More: Is Trinity Rodman playing in NWSL Championship? Washington Spirit star’s status Trinity Rodman health is biggest win The biggest question heading into the season was whether or not Rodman would remain in Washington, D.C. That was answered when Rodman signed a deal reportedly worth more than $2 million a year through 2028, making her the highest-paid player in league history. The deal was made possible by the high-impact player rule , which allows clubs to exceed the league's salary cap by up to $1 million. (The rule is nicknamed the "Rodman Rule.") She was worth every penny. "Obviously, it was incredibly important for us to keep Trinity in this league," NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman said. "The fact that she's competing in the championship, again, is poetic given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars, and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field, and we are excited that she brings that to our game." The next biggest question mark is whether she could put together a full season. Between cheering on her beau, Ben Shelton , throughout his run to the US Open final and walking the runway at the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show , Rodman appeared in every single game for the Spirit this year. Spirit head coach Adrián González said it's no secret this is "100% her best season." "Not just because of the numbers... being available, I think for me, that's been key," he said after the Spirit's Decision Day win over the Chicago Red Stars, where Rodman scored a goal in the 2-0 win. item.title: Dwyane Wade Points To Davion Mitchell As Heat’s Turnaround Spark
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat have turned their season around in a big way after a rough start. They lost four games in a row to begin the year, but now they have won nineof their last eleven. That includes a current five-game win streak that has fans feeling good again. Dwyane Wade believes the change comes down to one specific player who stepped up when the team needed him most. Wade says Davion Mitchell has been the key catalyst for this new run of success. “I think we all are big fans of what Davion Mitchell is doing for the Miami Heat right now,” Wade said via Wade’s WY Network, according to Heavy.com . Mitchell was brought in because the team thought they might need another point guard, but now the roster feels solid. He is acting as the conductor on offense, which lets stars like Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo play their best. The stats back up Wade’s take, as Mitchell is averaging 17.2 points and nine assists per game over his first 15 contests. The team is also 1.9 points better per 100 possessions when he is on the floor. Depth Remains a Big Concern Despite the winning, the roster still has holes that could cause trouble later in the season. Draymond Green warned that the Heat lack the depth needed to be truly dangerous in the Eastern Conference. He noted that the team is always just one injury away from things going the wrong way without enough backup options. Green admitted he is enjoying watching Klay Thompson score 15.3 points per game with 43.2 percent shooting from deep, but he still sees a risk. The front office will likely need to find more help before the trade deadline to fix this issue. Plans to Bring Back a Favorite While the team looks for new depth, they are also thinking about bringing back old friends. Heat insider Ethan Skolnick reported that the organization wants to re-sign Jaime Jaquez Jr. as soon as he becomes available again. Skolnick heard from sources within the team that Pat Riley and the front office will “make a play to try and bring him back.” Jaquez was a fan favorite during his three seasons in Miami before he was traded to Milwaukee in a blockbuster deal for Giannis. He is now averaging 15 points per game for the Bucks and will hit restricted free agency in 2027. Skolnick also mentioned that the Heat could have future interest in reuniting with Kasparas Jakucionis once he reaches his rookie extension. Since Jaquez is already familiar with coach Erik Spoelstra’s system, his return would instantly energize Miami’s bench. The former forward is shooting a career-high 42.3 percent from three-point range this season. The Heat will undoubtedly try to find more depth to support their current five-game win streak.

item.title: Flyers Make Significant Line Changes Ahead of Saturday Matchup vs. Canadiens; Insight & Opinion
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It seems like winning Thursday’s game wasn’t enough for Philadelphia Flyers head coach Rick Tocchet . After having to erase a 3-goal deficit to leave Ottawa with a win, Tocchet has thrown the forward lines in a blender ahead of Saturday’s showdown against the Montreal Canadiens. While the lines weren’t perfect, the Flyers had something good going with Denver Barkey playing alongside Sean Couturier and Noel Acciari. Matvei Michkov and Noah Cates seemed to have some real chemistry with Porter Martone. After some reshuffling of the lines, the Flyers have gotten away from those groups. Now, the Flyers are rolling out a whole new forward group, with completely different lines. Jackie Spiegel of the Philadelphia Inquirer reported the team’s lines at morning skate on Saturday; the new lines look like this: Tyson Foerster – Christian Dvorak – Travis Konecny Porter Martone – Denver Barkey – Owen Tippett Cole Knuble – Noah Cates – Matvei Michkov Trevor Zegras – Sean Couturier – Noel Acciari It’s quite a different look for the Flyers. Trevor Zegras , who is tied for the 2nd most points on the team with 15 and is 2nd in goals with 5, moved from being the top-line center to the 4th-line left wing. Christian Dvorak jumped up to Zegras’ spot, with Denver Barkey , a player who seemed to fit that 4th line so well, is now the team’s 2C. Porter Martone and Cole Knuble flip-flopped lines, with Martone now on the second line and Knuble on the 3rd. The defensive pairings were lightly changed up as well. Per Spiegel’s report, Jamie Drysdale and Rasmus Ristolainen have flipped spots. The pairings now look like this: Travis Sanheim – Rasmus Ristolainen Cam York – Jamie Drysdale Nick Seeler – Oliver Bonk The 3rd pair remains the same. Overall, I don’t mind the defensive changes. Cam York seemed to be just fine offensively with Jamie Drysdale on Thursday after the in-game switch. I am not too worried about that, as York seems to be finding his way again. However, the forward changes are a bit alarming to me. While it is the 4th line, the Barkey – Couturier – Acciari line has been the one consistent line for the Flyers. Even when the rest of the team is not going, they are. Barkey just fit the play style of Acciari and Couturier, and brought the best out of both. I thought he elevated that line. The Wizards are still at the bottom of the Play-In picture at 6-11, even after getting Trae Young and Anthony Davis , while the Jazz have already lost most of their starting frontcourt to injuries and are sitting at 3-13. And with both teams trying to figure out what to do next, there could be an interesting trade involving two former All-Stars who are still making a lot of money. Davis is playing some of his best basketball in years with Washington, but the Wizards have a younger center in Alex Sarr and still need much better shooting around their players . Utah, meanwhile, has Lauri Markkanen on a huge contract, although his recent injury and disappointing start have made his future a little more difficult to figure out. So, what if the Wizards and Jazz decided to swap their veteran stars? Washington could finally get the shooting it needs, while Utah would add one of the best defensive big men in the NBA and get out of Markkanen’s longer contract. It wouldn’t be a simple decision for either team, especially with how much money both players are making, but there are some good reasons why this trade could work. The Blockbuster Trade Idea Washington Wizards Receive: Lauri Markkanen, Josh Green, 2029 second-round pick (via Jazz), 2031 second-round pick (via Jazz) Utah Jazz Receive: Anthony Davis The idea here is pretty simple. Washington gets a younger forward who can shoot next to Trae Young and Alex Sarr, while Utah gets an All-Star big man who can help its defense and doesn’t have three more guaranteed seasons on his contract. Markkanen is making $46.1 million this season, while Josh Green adds another $14.7 million, giving the Jazz around $60.8 million in outgoing salaries. Davis is earning $58.5 million, so the money is close enough to make this a reasonable starting point for a trade, and I think the two second-round picks would be fair compensation for Washington taking on the longer contract, especially with Markkanen currently injured and not playing at the same level he did last season. Why The Wizards Should Consider Trading Anthony Davis Washington made two major moves to get Young and Davis, hoping its young players could learn from two established stars while the team started winning more games. But the Wizards are only 5-11, and even with Davis having a very good season, they’re still struggling to score a lot. And the biggest problem is probably their three-point shooting. item.description: Fantastic four for Celtic against St Mirren Scottish Premiership Saturday, November 21, 2026 Celtic Park CELTIC…4 (Oxlade-Chamberlain 33, Durán 40, McCowan 42, McGregor 63) ST MIRREN…1 (Phillips 70) Celtic have returned from the international break with a convincing and deserved 4-1 win against St Mirren at Celtic Park, with goals from Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Camilo Durán, Luke McCowan and Callum McGregor securing the points for the Hoops. The Bhoys looked to have got off to the best possible start when Camilo Durán found the back of the net with a headed finish in the ninth minute after a good cross from Kieran Tierney, but the offside flag cut the celebrations short and the scoreline remained level. Durán had the ball in the net again five minutes later after latching on to the rebounded ball following Jota’s saved attempt on goal, but once again the offside flag denied the Colombian the opener. Celtic were in control of the match in the first 30 minutes, with Jota and Yang giving St Mirren some defensive work to do with their positive play on the wings. The visitors had to defend in numbers to deny the Hoops a clear chance at goal. With 33 minutes on the clock, the opener which Celtic deserved was delivered by Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain following some nice play on the wing from Yang. The Korean pulled away from St Mirren’s Declan John before cutting the ball back to Oxlade-Chamberlain, who produced a tidy finish from 12 yards out to put Celtic 1-0 ahead. That lead should have been doubled five minutes later when Yang burst through on goal with the ball at his feet. With just the keeper to beat, the winger could have pulled the trigger, but instead he was unselfish and tried to square it to Durán, giving the St Mirren defence a chance to clear the ball. Durán didn’t have to wait long for his next opportunity, however, and when Kieran Tierney sent a brilliant cross in to the box from the right wing a few moments later, the Colombian was on hand six yards out from goal to knock the ball by Jacob Champan and make it 2-0 to Celtic. It was 3-0 soon after, and once again Kieran Tierney was the provider, this time with a pass inside from the left wing to find Luke McCowan in the box. McCowan made no mistake as he lashed the ball into the net to put the Hoops three ahead. Early in the second half, Sam Johnstone was called in to action after Ismael Kabia sent a powerful shot towards the bottom corner from outside the box. item.title: Dwayne ‘The Rock’ Johnson offers sage advice for players in transfer portal/NIL era on ‘College GameDay’ set
item.description: Credit: Peter Casey-USA TODAY Sports Dwayne ‘The Rock’ Johnson offers sage advice for players in transfer portal/NIL era on ‘College GameDay’ set appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ahead of WWE Survivor Series on Thanksgiving weekend, Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson appeared at his alma mater , the University of Miami, as College GameDay’s celebrity guest picker. Miami is set to face off in a high-stakes battle with Virginia Tech on Saturday as the season nears its end and their hopes of making the college football playoffs continue. Awesome to hear from @TheRock on how he’s overcome adversity and his advice for college athletes 👏 pic.twitter.com/qZ4su4lAUA — Kirk Herbstreit (@KirkHerbstreit) November 21, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Asked by Kirk Herbstreit what he’d tell players tempted to leave when they hit adversity, Johnson said he understood the feeling, since he faced a similar moment at Miami. “I get that, and I understand that, because I went through that when I was here at Miami, ’cause I felt like, ‘Man, is this the right place for me?’ I got injured my freshman year, redshirt freshman year. I was backup to Russell Maryland, who’s one of the greats of all time. I got hurt, and then my career changed after that time when I got hurt. And I wish I had at least the option of a portal.” He said that while the transfer portal is an opportunity, players should pause before reacting, and he encouraged them to talk to people. “But what I like to tell these young athletes today is, while the portal is there for an opportunity, take a moment. Don’t react to what’s happening around you. Take your time. Take a breath. Respond. Talk to people. Don’t hold it all in, by the way, like I did, like we did. We didn’t have mental health education back then. We had ‘suck it up’ and live with it.” Johnson said he supports players making the most of the opportunities available to them, including financially. “I would say that. But again, it’s tough because there’s a lot of opportunity out there, and I’m an advocate for every student athlete, football players for sure, ’cause I was one, to get as much as you can. And make as much money as you can, too, as well. ‘Cause there’s a cap there, and it will end.” Johnson was a defensive tackle who played for Miami from 1990 to 1994. While with the Hurricanes, he was a part of the national championship team in 1991. He played 39 games and finished his career with 4.5 sacks and 77 tackles. item.title: Justice for Denny Hamlin? Insider Drops Bold Points-Lead Proposal to Fix NASCAR’s Chase Reset
item.description: ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Denny Hamlin had done almost everything NASCAR could ask of a regular-season champion. He had built an 89-point lead, secured the No. 1 seed before the regular season ended, and given Joe Gibbs Racing a reason to feel confident heading into the Chase. Then came the points reset. Suddenly, that commanding advantage was worth just 25 points over the second seed. The difference between Denny Hamlin’s season-long dominance and his actual postseason advantage has now prompted an interesting discussion about whether NASCAR is rewarding its best-performing drivers enough. Andrew Kurland offered a possible solution on PRN Live , suggesting that NASCAR should retain its 25-point minimum but allow the regular-season champion to carry back a percentage of their actual points advantage. “Say, all right, number one seed gets a minimum of a 25-point buffer, but any extra points, like if you win it by a race, or if you clinch or lock this thing up by a bunch, you get a percentage of those points back. So it’s not like a set thing. Like, that would give you incentive to keep dominating.” The distinction is important because NASCAR’s 2026 championship format was designed to bring consistency back into the title conversation. After 26 regular-season races, the top 16 drivers advance to a 10-race Chase. There are no eliminations or additional resets. Every point earned during those final 10 races counts toward the championship. NASCAR's Chase format has long frustrated top contenders. See what structural change could finally level the playing field for veterans like Hamlin. Subscribe for the latest playoff analysis. However, the initial reseeding changes the value of everything drivers accumulated beforehand. Denny Hamlin’s numbers show exactly why Kurland is questioning that approach. He finished the regular season with 1,027 points, while the gap between him and second-place Ryan Blaney stood at 89. Yet, after Daytona, Hamlin started The Chase with 2,100 points and Blaney with 2,075. The other 64 points of separation had effectively vanished. Under Kurland’s suggested model, half of Denny Hamlin’s 89-point advantage would have given him approximately 45 points instead of 25. That is an additional 20 points to protect across the 10-race championship battle. More importantly, every extra point earned during the regular season would have had a purpose beyond simply securing the top seed. Kurland also pointed out that such a system could make the Daytona finale more meaningful for drivers already secure in the Chase.
